forecasts.label: Interest payable

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Cherwell forecasts £0.436m overspend, against a £0.275m underspend in June
news_drafts.lead:
Cherwell District Council's Executive is told that the council expects to end the financial year £0.436m over budget, 1.4% of its £32.267m budget. In June it was forecasting an underspend of £0.275m, so the forecast has moved by £0.711m in two months, according to the August budget monitoring report (the in-year check of spending against budget).

Two areas account for most of the change. Finance is forecasting a £0.500m overspend on housing benefit. Place and Regeneration is forecasting £0.402m over, mainly because Development Management, the planning service, is £0.369m short on income. That service has a £0.372m budget and is forecast to spend £0.741m. It was £0.074m over in June, so the gap has widened by £0.295m since then. The paper puts the pressure on Finance at "£0.500m" and Development Management at "£0.369m".

Some of this is offset. Neighbourhood Services is forecasting an underspend of £0.115m. Executive Matters, the budget heading that carries the council's treasury management (how it invests spare cash and manages borrowing), is £0.249m under, because interest rates are higher than the council forecast.

findings.paper_title: Council Tax Empty Home and Second Home Premium Policy 2026/2027
findings.paper_url: https://modgov.cherwell.gov.uk/documents/s64419/Council Tax Empty and Second Homes report 2026 Executive.pdf
findings.headline: Cherwell reduced Council Tax empty homes premium threshold from two years to one year from 1 April 2025
findings.detail: The council implemented the change permitted by the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023, bringing properties into premium scope sooner. Properties now face graduated premiums: 100% for 1–5 years empty, 200% for 5–10 years, 300% for 10+ years. This is already in effect.
findings.matters: Demonstrates active use of available statutory powers to expand the tax base and accelerate revenue collection from empty properties.
findings.figures: 1 year or more unoccupied threshold; 100%, 200%, 300% premiums by duration; effective from 1 April 2025
findings.quote: Cherwell District Council will charge a premium once a property has remained unoccupied and unfurnished for one year or more from 1 April 2025.

findings.paper_title: Council Tax Empty Home and Second Home Premium Policy 2026/2027
findings.paper_url: https://modgov.cherwell.gov.uk/documents/s64419/Council Tax Empty and Second Homes report 2026 Executive.pdf
findings.headline: Cherwell will apply 100% Council Tax premium to unoccupied substantially furnished second homes from 1 April 2027
findings.detail: The council approved this new policy in February 2026 and published statutory notice in the 2025-26 council tax charges, exceeding the 12-month statutory notice requirement. The premium will apply automatically to qualifying second homes from the implementation date, creating a new revenue stream affecting the council tax base.
findings.matters: This introduces a material new council tax revenue stream that will affect the authority's budget and financial position from April 2027.
findings.figures: 100% premium; 1 April 2027; 12-month statutory notice published in 2025-26 charges
findings.quote: Cherwell District Council will, from 1 April 2027, automatically apply a Council Tax second home premium of 100% on unoccupied second homes.

findings.paper_title: Reserves Draw Down Cherwell Futures cover report
findings.headline: Planning Service Improvement Programme allocated £0.370m with benefits still unquantified; validation pending November 2026
findings.detail: The Planning Service Improvement Programme is allocated £0.370m in 2026/27 transformation funding, but shows £0m in identified cashable savings, additional income, or released capacity in the September 2026 full business case position. Benefits quantification is deferred to after a DEF fit-gap assessment and process redesign completing November 2026. The programme business case is due formal Executive approval January 2027.
findings.matters: One of three core transformation pillars is committed with benefit validation delayed; if planned benefits do not materialise, the overall £3.1m–£3.6m claimed saving is materially lower.
findings.figures: £0.370m allocation for Planning 2026/27; £0m identified savings at September 2026; benefits validation due after 30 November 2026
findings.quote: cashable savings, additional income, released capacity and cost avoidance will be validated after the DEF fit-gap assessment and process redesign (due Nov 2026)

findings.paper_title: Reserves Draw Down Cherwell Futures cover report
findings.headline: £0.330m transformation funding depends on Customer Front Door restructures delivering savings by 1 January 2027
findings.detail: The additional £0.330m transformation funding depends on unbudgeted in-year savings from Customer Front Door restructures, with implementation due 1 January 2027. Finance commentary flags that if savings are not delivered, the council will still incur the transformation costs but must find alternative funding. Further, if restructures do not match the approved business case scope, ongoing benefits will be lower while costs continue.
findings.matters: Shows structural risk where programme costs are committed dependent on operational restructuring execution; failed delivery creates a funding gap and loss of expected ongoing savings in the same financial year.
findings.figures: £0.330m unbudgeted savings requirement; restructures due 1 January 2027
findings.quote: These savings are wholly dependent on the services identified implementing restructures in line with the proposals from the Customer Front Door Project. If the restructures are not designed to at least match those identified as part of the approved business case then the ongoing savings will also be less than anticipated whilst the council will incur the ongoing costs.

findings.paper_title: Reserves Draw Down Cherwell Futures cover report
findings.headline: Transformation programme funding gap of £0.330m identified after reserve approval; now to be covered from unbudgeted in-year savings
findings.detail: The Cherwell Futures Reserve of £1.1m was approved in October 2025 to fund interim resource and preparatory work. Full Business Cases developed by September 2026 have identified additional £0.330m in unforeseen costs for systems (new telephony and website) and capability building. This shortfall is proposed to be funded from unbudgeted in-year savings from the Customer Front Door programme restructuring, contingent on those changes being in place by 1 January 2027.
findings.matters: Shows how transformation costs can exceed initial estimates even with detailed business case development; funding gaps are addressed through contingent operational savings rather than additional reserves.
findings.figures: £1.1m original reserve approved October 2025; £0.330m additional requirement identified; £1.997m total 2026/27 allocation
findings.quote: The original request for Reserves in October 2025 was to fund targeted investment to cover the costs of essential interim roles and specialist expertise... Through this, the new intelligence and analysis that has been undertaken has identified investment required in systems (both new and upgrades), external consultancy support (Route Optimisation, etc), and gaps in capability and capacity to deliver from within existing services. These additional requirements are in the region of £0.330m
